60635.name: Logic and Computability
60635.recommendedPriorKnowledge: In order to follow this class you need to have successfully finished the Introduction to Logic or a similar course. If you are not sure whether you fulfill the entry requirements of this class, please contact the teacher. Please make sure that you refresh your knowledge of the material covered in the Introduction to Logic before the start of this course. There will be little room to do so after the course has started. Look in particular at Natural Deduction and the notions/notation from set-theory that were introduced in that class.

61024.name: AI in Society: Safety, Regulation, Fairness

sourceUse: Retrieved UvA’s programme-specific Part B via the official student regulations index and inspected Articles B-4.1, B-4.4, B-4.5, B-4.8 and the transition tables. The first-year table applies explicitly to cohort 2026–2027. The year-two and year-three tables are explicitly for cohorts 2025–2026 and 2024–2025 and match the dated catalogue. The public grid and downloadable 2026–2027 diagram instead show Mathematics for Algorithms at 6 EC, Software Engineering and Logic in year two, and 30 EC open plus 6 EC compulsory Robots that Learn in year three. The transition table says Mathematics for Algorithms, Logic and Software Engineering return as year-two courses from 2027–2028, but lists Mathematics for Algorithms at 5 EC and does not set a complete new-cohort upper-year grid. The forward-dated catalogue calls repeated the older grid and supplied no cohort-specific confirmation.
components: AI in Society: Safety, Regulation, Fairness
Oriëntatie op studie en loopbaan KI semester 1

UvA’s regulations require completion of the first and second years before the graduation project. The project is 18 EC in both published schedules.
progression: Article B-4.8 and the project entry require both 60 EC years before the 18 EC project, subject to exceptional dispensation. First-year calculus and linear algebra precede optimisation, then statistics and cognitive modelling, machine learning and problem solving. The 24 EC that differ across the upper-year versions are withheld from the partial record. The shared 96 EC are corroborated across the grids; the unresolved cohort attribution prevents a full comparison.
